An earlier pass here recorded 'Vilna then Odessa' from catalogue metadata; that was WRONG and is corrected. Reading the TITLE PAGES themselves (archive.org/download/<id>/<id>_djvu.txt) shows the imprints carry TWO separate lines, and the catalogue collapsed them into one, inverting the sense: nybc204446 (1897) line 101 'בהוצאת האחים בלאמניצקי באדעססא' then line 103 'ווילנא'; nybc202364 (1909) line 95 'בהוצאת האחים בלעטניצקי. באדעססא' then line 98 'ווילנא. תרסט'; nybc214795 (1895) line 153 'הזכות נמכר לצמיתות להאחים בלעטניצקי מויס באדעססא' ('the rights were sold in perpetuity to the Bletnitski Brothers OF ODESSA') then line 162 'ווילנא'. So באדעססא names the FIRM and ווילנא names the PLACE OF PRINTING; IA's publisher field reads 'Ṿilna : ha-Aḥim Bleṭnitsḳi', which is the opposite of what the page says. NATURE: a bookshop that published and commissioned printing, never (on this evidence) a press of its own — 'פערלאג און אייגענטהום פון בוכהאנדלונג' (farlag and property of the bookshop), 'בית מסחר הספרים' (book-trading house); the 1911 play was printed at Bialik & Borishkin's shop in Odessa. Business model: buying rights outright and reissuing popular Yiddish fiction, which is why its name sits over books printed in other cities. ACTIVITY c.1878-1918, Warsaw -> Odessa; the 1878 Warsaw imprint names the brothers as Heym (Chaim) and Perets Bletnitski, though that is a single source and early enough that the 1900s firm may be sons or younger brothers. Published Shomer and Linetzky, Yiddish drama and operetta (the theatrical connection: Lebedig un lustig 1914, Di hayrat-komedye 1911, Madam Freylein), Klausner's 4-volume Historiyah Yisreelit (1915), a Hebrew children's library after I. B. Levner's death, and a 1918 Haggadah. MINT AS ONE ORG seated in ODESSA — not Vilna — with both clusters attached. OPEN: whether a Vilna shopfront ever existed. On this evidence no; the Leksikon's own Shomer bibliography lists 'Vilna: Bletnitski' but was likely compiled from these same two-line title pages, so it is probably the same error propagating, not independent evidence. An Odessa or Vilna commercial register would settle it.

publisher audit 2026-10-10 (P148): minted db 2661 בוכהאַנדלונג געברידער בלעטניצקי and aligned here. RESOLVED 2026-10-10: the firm is ODESSA, and the Leksikon was right all along. An earlier pass here recorded 'Vilna then Odessa' from catalogue metadata; that was WRONG and is corrected. Reading the TITLE PAGES themselves (archive.org/download/<id>/<id>_djvu.txt) shows the imprints carry TWO separate lines, and the catalogue collapsed them into one, inverting the sense: nybc204446 (1897) line 101 'בהוצאת האחים בלאמניצקי באדעססא' then line 103 'ווילנא'; nybc202364 (1909) line 95 'בהוצאת האחים בלעטניצקי. באדעססא' then line 98 'ווילנא. תרסט'; nybc214795 (1895) line 153 'הזכות נמכר לצמיתות להאחים בלעטניצקי מויס באדעססא' ('the rights were sold in perpetuity to the Bletnitski Brothers OF ODESSA') then line 162 'ווילנא'. So באדעססא names the FIRM and ווילנא names the PLACE OF PRINTING; IA's publisher field reads 'Ṿilna : ha-Aḥim Bleṭnitsḳi', which is the opposite of what the page says. NATURE: a bookshop that published and commissioned printing, never (on this evidence) a press of its own — 'פערלאג און אייגענטהום פון בוכהאנדלונג' (farlag and property of the bookshop), 'בית מסחר הספרים' (book-trading house); the 1911 play was printed at Bialik & Borishkin's shop in Odessa. Business model: buying rights outright and reissuing popular Yiddish fiction, which is why its name sits over books printed in other cities. ACTIVITY c.1878-1918, Warsaw -> Odessa; the 1878 Warsaw imprint names the brothers as Heym (Chaim) and Perets Bletnitski, though that is a single source and early enough that the 1900s firm may be sons or younger brothers. Published Shomer and Linetzky, Yiddish drama and operetta (the theatrical connection: Lebedig un lustig 1914, Di hayrat-komedye 1911, Madam Freylein), Klausner's 4-volume Historiyah Yisreelit (1915), a Hebrew children's library after I. B. Levner's death, and a 1918 Haggadah. MINT AS ONE ORG seated in ODESSA — not Vilna — with both clusters attached. OPEN: whether a Vilna shopfront ever existed. On this evidence no; the Leksikon's own Shomer bibliography lists 'Vilna: Bletnitski' but was likely compiled from these same two-line title pages, so it is probably the same error propagating, not independent evidence. An Odessa or Vilna commercial register would settle it.
